newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC approves new NASD telemarketing rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC approves new NASD telemarketing rules.

text.p: NASD Regulation Inc said on Wednesday the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved its new telemarketing rules designed to protect investors from deceptive or abusive phone calls.

Under terms of the National Association of Securities Dealers' new rule, NASD member firms and their associated persons can no longer call an individual's residence to sell securities or related services before 0800 local or after 2100 local without the individual's prior consent, NASD said.
When a member firm's representative makes calls, he also must immediately give his name, firm and phone number and state that the purpose of the call is to sell securities or related products.

"Among other things, this rule ensures that anybody receiving a cold call from a broker will immediately know who they're dealing with and why," Michael Jones, director of the NASD office of individual investor services, said.

The new rule provides exemptions for calls to other broker dealers or to a firm's existing customer who has conducted a transaction or whose account has had activity -- such as earning interest or dividends -- in the past year, NASD said.
The rules would go into effect immediately, NASD said.
